bug_report:
Reassigning a repeated query parameter doesn't drop the old values. URL query params are an OrderedMultiDict, and for URL('http://x/?a=1&a=2'), after query_params['a'] = '9', getlist('a') returns ['1', '2', '9'] instead of ['9'] — the old values linger. It only shows up via getlist; url['a'] and round-tripping look fine. A failing repro is at tests/test_regression.py. Fix it without breaking existing behaviour.

Relevant project memory (from a past commit): dictutils: __setitem__ resets the underlying value list after _remove_all. _remove_all() clears the linked list and _map but leaves the underlying dict value list intact by design, so __setitem__ must reset it to [v] explicitly. Reusing add() there appends to the stale list and makes getlist(k) return the old values too (while __getitem__/iteration/todict hide it).
